ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French AML/CFT framework: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.561-1 to L.561-53 and R.561-1 et seq., implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; UBO declaration obligations: Articles L.561-2-1 and L.561-2-2 of the Code monétaire et financier, together with Decree No. 2018-57 of 31 January 2018 on the beneficial-ownership register; enforcement: French Penal Code Articles 324-1 et seq. and 421-1 et seq.; financial-intelligence supervision by TRACFIN.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national identity card of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or identity-issuing authority in the country of origin (national police, civil registry, or consular office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin country is a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization by the competent French consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address of each UBO and corporate representative (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local notary public or notarial public registrar in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official registry excerpt, certificate of incorporation or corporate register extract of each legal entity UBO/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry or commercial registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; a sworn French translation must accompany the original/extract

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation covering each equity contribution and the commercial purpose of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; not required if the letter originates from a French or European Economic Area regulated institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based KYC screening of all UBOs, shareholders and directors against (i) the French Ministry of Economy's national asset-freezing lists, (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list established under Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and its amending acts, (iii) the United Nations Security Council sanctions committees, and (iv) domestic judicial, electoral and professional-disqualification databases. PEPs are locally identified using TRACFIN guidance; every senior foreign PEP, and any PEP family member or close associate, is automatically classified as higher-risk and subjected to enhanced due diligence including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior-management approval, transaction monitoring, periodic review, and reporting to TRACFIN where suspicion arises. Where the corporate treasury will use USD payment channels, additional OFAC SDN and sectoral screening is maintained; where the app monetizes via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the payment providers require a clean sanctions profile and valid KYC identification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with name availability verified through the INPI official search portal (data.inpi.fr) and the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Infogreffe.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in the French commercial register and articles of association in French; the name may include a foreign-language element if transliterated into Latin script. A non-Latin script source name must be accompanied by a sworn French transliteration for RCS and INPI filing. The chosen name must not be confusingly similar to an existing RCS-denominated company, a pending French or EU trademark, or a protected trade name in France, and must not infringe public order or public morality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Because the validity window is thirty days, the incorporation package must be submitted before expiry; a reservation cannot be automatically extended and lapses thereafter. If the INPI/tribunal registrar rejects the name, the filer must (1) obtain a written rejection summary from the Guichet Unique, (2) review the exact conflicting RCS name or trademark, (3) seek a written no-objection/consent letter from the conflicting holder where applicable, and (4) either file an administrative clarification with the INPI within fifteen days of refusal or accept a modified name carrying a distinctive suffix, then resubmit through the Guichet Unique. If ministerial approval of a sensitive token is refused on public-order grounds, an appeal may be lodged before the Administrative Court of Paris within two months of notification; for ordinary commercial registry refusals, an action lies before the competent commercial court (tribunal de commerce).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is legally permissible for an SAS if contracted with an INPI-authorized commercial domiciliation company, for a maximum period of five years; a director's personal residence may also be used as registered office if the lease or condominium rules allow. For this interactive voice-chat and companion social application, the virtual-office route will be accepted for incorporation and RCS registration because no sectoral licence is required, but Apple IAP and Google Play Billing merchant-underwriting, French bank onboarding, and tax-prepaid payments will in practice require a documented operations centre, an appointed local compliance officer or tax representative, and a demonstrable ability to produce accounting and beneficial-ownership records on request.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk for the first full compliance year is 10%–15% (moderate) if the SAS uses only a virtual registered office and has no French employees; a physical visit may be triggered by an active bank or payment-provider counterparty risk review, VAT registration threshold breaches, or a TRACFIN report. If the company rents a small staffed operating office and files consistent VAT and income tax returns, the annual unannounced on-site inspection probability falls below 5%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), notably Articles L.227-1 to L.227-42 relating to Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS), and Articles R.210-1 to R.224-1 concerning registration formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry), acting through the Infogreffe single-window portal and the French RNE (Registre National des Entreprises) administered by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: M0 form (déclaration de création d'une entreprise) filed with the statuts (articles of association) and all required annexes, resulting in the issuance of the Extrait K-bis (RCS certificate).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS; capital amount is freely set in the articles. However, at least 50% of cash contribution must be fully paid up on subscription at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. No statutory escrow account is mandatory; funds may be deposited with a notary or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations if formation is completed without a notarial deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The founding shareholders and directors of [Company Name SAS] hereby resolve that: (i) all shares of the company shall be subscribed and issued in accordance with the executed statuts, and it is confirmed that 100% of the required paid-up capital has been duly deposited and made available; (ii) the registered office is hereby fixed at [Address], and the President of the company is authorized to execute the lease or other occupancy agreement for such office; (iii) [Name] is appointed as President of the Société par Actions Simplifiée with full powers to act on behalf of the company under French law; (iv) any other officers necessary for management shall be appointed as determined in the statuts; (v) the President is authorized to complete all filings with the competent Registry, to publish the mandatory legal notice, and to take all acts necessary for registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarizing the Statuts and Corporate Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Not verified by a government authority unless a notary is used; otherwise prepared by counsel and executed as a private deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SAS statuts (articles of association) reflecting the corporate purpose, share capital, share subscription, governance rules, and executive officers. Ensure non-resident ownership is permitted and no minimum capital blockade is intimated. If a notary is appointed, have the statuts executed in the notarial form and received by the notary for filing.
required_dossiers: Identification of shareholders and beneficial owners
Declaration of non-conviction and capacity of directors
Registered office lease or letter from the landlord consenting to the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry identifies an incomplete annex, correct the statuts or appointment documents and re-submit; use the Infogreffe helpdesk to obtain a checklist; file a formal opposition only after three refusals if the denial is unlawful.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening an Escrow and Depositing the Paid-Up Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, a notary, or any French licensed bank (when acting as receiver of funds).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked bank account in the name of the SAS in formation. Transfer the subscribed cash contributions (at least 50% of each cash subscription). Obtain a capital deposit certificate (certificat du dépositaire des fonds) from the bank or notary. This certificate must accompany the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of all founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the deposit certificate due to missing details, rectify the statuts or provide a revised ownership/beneficial owner list. Any delay in certificate issuance can be cured by using a notary as depositary instead.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Mandatory Legal Notice (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and publish a legal notice in a duly approved JAL containing the corporate name, form (SAS), registered office address, amount of share capital, corporate purpose, duration, directors/president details, and the RCS registration number where the company will be registered. Obtain the publication certificate from the JAL.
required_dossiers: Capital amount and cash contribution details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL notice is rejected, correct typographical mismatches or missing mandatory items and re-submit to an alternative approved journal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the M0 Incorporation File to the Commercial Court Registry (Infogreffe)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Infogreffe single online portal or local registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic M0 form, upload the statuts, publication certificate, capital deposit certificate, registered office documentation, and beneficial owner declaration. Pay the fixed statutory filing fee by card or bank transfer. Submit the file to the competent registry based on the registered office address.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Certificate of publication in a JAL
Declaration de bénéficiaires effectifs (beneficial owner form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query, respond within 15 days through the Infogreffe portal with corrected documents. If the application is rejected for formal defects, cure the defect and re-file. If erroneous refusal persists, file a petition with the President of the Commercial Court requesting registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Extrait K-bis and Post-Incorporation Announcements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RNE (Registre National des Entreprises) via INPI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Registry verifies the file, the company is registered in the RCS/RNE. The Registry issues the Extrait K-bis (equivalent of a corporate birth certificate). The company must then open a professional bank account, file tax registrations (SIREN/SIRET automatically assigned), and submit any sector-specific declarations to the RSI or the tax office.
required_dossiers: Valid proof of identity of President/shareholders
Copy of any lease or office agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed beyond the SLA, contact the RNE helpdesk or the Registry's quality mediation service. If the issued SIRET code contains errors, file a rectification request with the Registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the activity (interactive audio chatroom and companion social application) is purely digital and software-based, without physical manufacturing, heavy industrial operations, or installation requiring an industrial license. General workplace and fire safety rules are handled by local municipal authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating or manufacturing permit is required under French law for an audio streaming social platform; ordinary business declarations (e.g., declaration of data processing activity under GDPR/CNIL) are sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable — no EIA required because the company will not operate an IPPC (Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control) installation or enter the categories listed under the French Loi sur l'eau or the Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (no physical environmental footprint; operations are cloud-hosted VoIP and information services).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. The company shall, however, comply with all applicable workplace electrical safety and server-hosting standards if any office server room is established; otherwise, no wastewater, VOC, or waste-release thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Where the company occupies an office, the workplace must obtain a fire safety certificate (avis favorable de la commission de sécurité) if open to the public, as well as structural and electrical load clearances. For an office-only digital operation, no special occupational clearance is required beyond standard labor law compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de l'Industrie. Online portal: impots.gouv.fr; one-stop business registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique). Export customs authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French-established SAS: (1) file incorporation documents (statuts, registered office proof, identification of legal representative) through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; (2) INSEE automatically issues the 9-digit SIREN, the 14-digit SIRET and the RCS registration (Registre du commerce et des sociétés), generally within 1–5 business days; (3) the DGFiP automatically allocates the intra-Community VAT number (FR + 11 digits), normally transmitted with the INSEE registration; if not received within 15 days, apply via the DGFiP online service 'Demande d'attribution d'un numéro de TVA intracommunautaire'; (4) non-EU foreign entities without a French establishment must appoint a fiscal representative approved by the DGFiP and register through the SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) covering the representative's address; processing takes 4–8 weeks. The FR_SAS, being incorporated in France, does not require a representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - SAS is mandatorily subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) on its profits, with France's territoriality principle limiting non-resident branches to French-source business profits. Pass-through status is not available; there is no French equivalent of the US check-the-box election, and a SAS cannot elect transparent treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box exists in French law. The available elections are: (i) intégration fiscale (CGI Art. 223 A et seq.) - a SAS holding at least 95% of a subsidiary may elect group consolidation; (ii) option for the parent-subsidiary dividend exemption regime under CGI Arts. 145 and 216 (minimum 5% participation and 2-year holding period); (iii) waiver of the franchise en base to charge VAT (CGI Art. 293 B III) in order to recover input VAT; (iv) PE attribution rules are governed exclusively by applicable double tax treaties; (v) hybrid mismatch outcomes are imposed unilaterally by EU ATAD 2 (Directive (EU) 2016/1164, as transposed) and DAC 6 reporting, not by elective check-the-box mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), governed by CGI Arts. 256-259 D, transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise en base de TVA (CGI Art. 293 B): €37,500 (main) / €41,000 (tolerance) annual revenue for service businesses; €85,000 (main) / €91,900 (tolerance) for goods businesses; non-established foreign suppliers have no threshold. For the SAS, VAT registration is required in practice from the first day: (i) the core supplies to Apple and Google are intra-EU B2B digital services taxable in Ireland under the reverse charge, requiring a valid French VAT ID and VIES status; (ii) input VAT on app development, hosting and operating overhead is recoverable only if the business is registered, so the franchise waiver (CGI Art. 293 B III) is the recommended election; (iii) B2C consumer sales through app stores are not treated as the SAS's taxable supplies because the stores are deemed suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has enacted a mandatory e-invoicing/e-reporting reform: from 1 September 2026 all businesses must receive structured e-invoices and large enterprises/ETIs must issue them; from 1 September 2027 SMEs must also issue. Invoices must be issued, transmitted and archived in Factur-X, UBL or CII format through an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the public Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); transaction and payment data (e-reporting) are transmitted to DGFiP on the statutory transmission calendar. France does not operate a real-time per-invoice clearance or digital stamping system, but the automated PDP-to-PPF transmission creates an effective near-real-time audit trail. B2B invoices to Apple/Google fall within the e-invoicing scope; consumer sales via app stores are invoiced by the app stores themselves as deemed suppliers, with no separate e-invoicing obligation on the SAS for those end-consumer sales.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies can be zero-rated or outside French VAT scope where the place of supply is not France: (1) B2B digital voice-streaming services supplied to Apple Distribution International Ltd (VAT IE9700053D) and Google Commerce Ltd (VAT IE6388047V), both established in Ireland, are taxable in Ireland under the reverse charge (CGI Art. 259-1; Directive 2006/112/EC Arts. 44 and 196), so no French VAT at 20% is due; (2) services supplied to business customers established outside the EU are entirely outside French VAT scope; (3) B2C sales to French/EU end-users made through the Apple App Store and Google Play are deemed supplies by the platforms (art. 14a VAT Directive), so the SAS charges no French VAT on those sales. To sustain the zero-rated/outside-scope treatment, the SAS must maintain two non-contradictory items of evidence of the customer's location (IP address, billing address, BIN of payment card, mobile country code, bank details), valid VIES-confirmed VAT IDs of the Irish customers, signed marketplace agreements, invoices mentioning 'autoliquidation par le preneur' or 'hors champ de TVA', and app-store payout statements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane - DELTA/DXE) - relevant only if physical goods are bundled; not applicable to pure digital voice-streaming services
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill - applicable only to physical export shipments; not applicable to digital services
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit evidence - App Store Connect Payout Reports and Google Play payout confirmations evidencing remittance of net proceeds after 15%-30% platform commission
B2B service agreement with Apple Distribution International Ltd (VAT IE9700053D) and Google Commerce Ltd (VAT IE6388047V), confirming the deemed-supplier marketplace structure
Reverse-charge tax invoices issued to Apple/Google under CGI Art. 259-1, stating 'Autoliquidation par le preneur' and displaying the SAS's French VAT ID and the Irish VAT IDs of the customers

Digital export substantiation file: IP address logs, billing/postal address data, payment method BIN data, mobile country codes and app-store transaction logs maintained per EU Implementing Regulation (EU) 2013/1042
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the deemed-supplier/reverse-charge structure fails documentation audit or is recharacterized as artificial (e.g., Apple/Google marketplace arrangement set aside as abusive), DGFiP will reassess 20% VAT on gross revenue, add late interest (CGI Art. 1727: 0.20% per month) and apply a 40% penalty for understatement (CGI Art. 1729) or 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (manœuvres frauduleuses). Inadequate export/outside-scope documentation triggers invoice-formality fines under CGI Art. 1737 (up to €750 per invoice under the e-invoicing mandate) and a 50% documentary-inaccuracy assessment where an exemption is unjustified. Deliberate use of false export documents constitutes criminal tax fraud under CGI Art. 1741, punishable by up to 5 years' imprisonment and a €500,000 fine, with publication of sanctions. Recovery is enforced by avis de mise en recouvrement, tax liens, and abus de droit recharacterization under LPF Art. L.64 with the 80% penalty applicable to connected parties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: European Central Bank for euro-area monetary policy and payment-system oversight; Banque de France for French central-banking functions, payment-system operations, balance-of-payments reporting and certain regulatory duties; French Treasury Directorate General (Direction générale du Trésor) for French external-financial policy and applicable capital-movement controls; Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution for supervision of French credit institutions and payment institutions; Autorité des marchés financiers for financial-market and investment-services supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro. Current-account convertibility is unrestricted, subject to ordinary bank compliance, sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, tax reporting and documentation of the underlying transaction. Capital-account movements are generally unrestricted within the European Union and under applicable treaty and OECD principles. A French SAS may receive foreign shareholder capital, intercompany funding and trade receipts in euros or foreign currencies and may remit dividends, interest, royalties, service fees and loan principal to non-residents, subject to corporate-law approvals, distributable-profit limitations, withholding-tax analysis, treaty eligibility, transfer-pricing support, beneficial-owner verification, anti-abuse rules, sanctions screening and bank payment controls. France does not impose a general foreign-exchange licence, mandatory profit-repatriation timetable, capital repatriation approval or routine conversion requirement. Cash transfers involving sanctioned jurisdictions, restricted persons, dual-use goods, designated sectors or unusual structures may be blocked, reported or require a specific legal analysis. Banks may request contracts, invoices, board resolutions, tax evidence, source-of-funds records and proof of economic purpose before executing or releasing a payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts, be converted voluntarily, or be applied to permitted treasury and settlement purposes. The company should retain invoices, transport or service-delivery evidence, customer contracts, payment confirmations and accounting records. Cross-border payment and balance-of-payments information may be collected or reported by banks, the Banque de France or other competent authorities under applicable statistical, prudential, tax, AML and sanctions frameworks. Cash or equivalent movements of EUR 10,000 or more into or out of the European Union are subject to customs declaration rules; this does not apply to ordinary bank transfers but remains relevant to physical cash and certain bearer instruments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank, a subsidiary of Crédit Agricole S.A.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; capital-deposit availability depends on the selected Crédit Agricole regional bank and its corporate onboarding policy

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group banking network, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne entities
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account; contracting entity depends on the selected regional institution

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment accounts and operating collections; low to medium for initial SAS share-capital deposit escrow. An electronic-money institution or payment institution authorised in France or another European Economic Area state may provide payment services under its licence and applicable passporting or local-registration framework, but it is not a French bank and generally cannot provide a statutory bank capital-deposit certificate unless the receiving institution and formation professional accept the arrangement. Safeguarding, client-money segregation, transaction limits, restricted activities, safeguarding-bank dependencies, sanctions screening and onboarding restrictions apply. Offshore digital EMIs outside the European Economic Area cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to French customers without an applicable French or EEA authorisation, passport, local establishment or other valid exemption. The SAS should maintain a domestic bank account for statutory capital, payroll, tax, regulated collections and payment-continuity purposes, with an EMI used as a supplementary rail after legal and contractual verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that every director physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank can reliably verify the company, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorised signatories, identity documents, address, tax residence, source of funds, business activity and expected transaction profile. Banks may require a video interview, certified or apostilled documents, French translations, wet-ink signatures, in-person attendance or a French professional intermediary based on risk, foreign ownership, complex control chains, non-resident management, high-risk jurisdictions, virtual-office use, unusual funding or inconsistent business information. The statutory capital deposit process requires an account provider willing to issue the deposit certificate for the SAS incorporation file; attendance requirements are institution-specific.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or director with an opaque ownership chain, nominee shareholder, trust, foundation or unexplained holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate extracts for every entity in the chain; constitutional documents; ownership chart identifying each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and residential-address evidence; director and shareholder registers; tax-residence information; beneficial-owner declaration; explanation of control rights; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds records; board or shareholder resolutions authorising the investment; and, where relevant, legal opinions or trust documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital, shareholder loan funding or recurring foreign remittances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription and shareholder-loan agreements; bank statements showing origin of funds; audited financial statements or tax returns of the funding entity; sale-of-asset or dividend evidence where applicable; upstream board approvals; payment purpose and remitter identification; transaction chronology; accounting entries; and a written funds-flow memorandum reconciling the amount, currency and beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Voice-streaming or social-app business model perceived as high-risk because of user-generated content, virtual goods, creator payouts, minors, adult content, gambling-like features or rapid cross-border micropayments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product and revenue description; platform terms; content-moderation and notice-and-action procedures; age-assurance controls; prohibited-content policy; creator and merchant onboarding standards; chargeback and refund policy; payment-flow diagram; customer and creator geography; expected monthly volumes and average ticket size; sanctions and fraud controls; data-protection governance; consumer-protection assessment; and evidence that Apple and Google payment policies are followed where their billing rails are used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between registered activity, ISIC classification, website, invoices, payment descriptors and expected account activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence; articles of association; business plan; product screenshots or controlled demonstration; domain ownership evidence; commercial contracts; platform and technology agreements; sample invoices; payment-processor agreements; customer acquisition model; management biographies; projected transaction matrix by currency, country, counterparty and purpose; and a written reconciliation of all business descriptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual registered office, non-French operating location or inability to demonstrate French economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or domiciliation agreement; proof of operating premises where applicable; employee or contractor records; French tax registrations; management and development-service agreements; board-meeting records; local suppliers and customer contracts; accounting records; French telephone and website details; explanation of the SAS's functions; and evidence distinguishing legitimate remote operations from mailbox-only activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payments involving high-risk, sanctioned or embargoed countries, payment intermediaries, cryptoasset businesses or unexplained third-party payers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty ownership and sanctions-screening results; end-use and end-customer information; contracts and invoices; shipping or service evidence; payment-chain map; licence or regulatory status of intermediaries; enhanced due-diligence file; internal approval record; transaction-monitoring rules; and documented refusal or escalation procedures for prohibited transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple payment accounts, rapid pass-through flows, third-party collections or significant cash-equivalent activity inconsistent with a software platform
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; account inventory; reconciled bank statements; cash-flow forecast; segregation-of-duties matrix; payment approval rules; explanation of marketplace or creator-settlement flows; reserve and chargeback methodology; processor settlement reports; general-ledger reconciliation; and evidence that customer funds are not unlawfully treated as safeguarded funds or deposit-taking activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residence, FATCA, CRS or beneficial-owner information incomplete or inconsistent with bank records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax-identification evidence; CRS self-certification; FATCA classification and forms where applicable; VAT registration evidence if applicable; corporate tax-residence analysis; beneficial-owner declarations; director tax-residence confirmations; and reconciliation of legal, tax and banking addresses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a regulated EEA bank or authorised payment institution with a French or euro-area account capable of receiving shareholder funds. The remitter should be the identified shareholder or documented lender, and the payment reference should identify the legal basis, such as SAS share-capital subscription, share-premium contribution or shareholder loan. For incorporation, route subscribed share capital to a designated capital-deposit account and obtain the deposit certificate required for registration; release the funds to the SAS operational account after registration and delivery of the registration evidence. For post-incorporation funding, use executed subscription or loan documents, board or shareholder approvals where required, transfer-pricing support for related-party debt, and a reconciled funds-flow schedule. Provide the bank with UBO information, source-of-funds evidence, tax-residence data, expected payment volumes and relevant contracts before remittance. SEPA Credit Transfer is appropriate for euro payments within the SEPA area; SWIFT cross-border wires are appropriate for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. Use accurate ISO currency, beneficiary, BIC, IBAN, purpose and remitter data. Do not split payments to avoid review, use undisclosed third-party remitters or route funds through personal accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro-denominated supplier and service payments in SEPA, use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer where supported, subject to bank limits and fraud controls. For international payments, use SWIFT customer-credit transfers, commonly represented by an MT103 legacy format or its ISO 20022 successor message, with complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, purpose and sanctions-screening data. For higher-value or documentary trade transactions, use a commercial documentary letter of credit issued or confirmed by a regulated bank, with compliant presentation of invoices, transport documents, insurance documents and other stipulated documents. Use documentary collections, open-account payments, bank guarantees or standby letters of credit only after counterparty, country and enforceability review. Reconcile every settlement to the contract, invoice, purchase order, goods or service evidence and general ledger. Maintain controls for beneficiary changes, dual approval, segregation of duties, payment release, sanctions screening, fraud monitoring, chargebacks and failed or returned payments. Apple App Store and Google Play billing settlements should be reconciled to platform statements, withholding or indirect-tax deductions, reserves, refunds, chargebacks and the contractual settlement currency; direct user payment processing should not bypass platform rules or applicable French and EU payment, consumer, AML and tax requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorised bank or investment firm, used to hedge documented forecast or committed exposures and supported by a treasury policy, exposure schedule, counterparty limit and confirmation controls.

Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity, currency conversion and maturity management, subject to documented commercial exposure, counterparty credit limits, collateral terms and applicable regulatory documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or where deliverable settlement is unavailable, subject to eligible-counterparty access, benchmark and fixing provisions, cash-settlement documentation, sanctions screening and local-market restrictions. NDFs are generally unnecessary for ordinary EUR exposure but may be relevant to non-euro supplier or platform flows.

Currency options, collars and other permitted OTC or exchange-traded derivatives may be used only where the bank confirms suitability, classification, disclosure, valuation, collateral, accounting and applicable EMIR or MiFID requirements. Avoid speculative trading unrelated to identified business exposures.

For an SAS, establish written hedging authority, permitted-instrument rules, hedge-designation and accounting procedures, independent confirmation, valuation and collateral monitoring, counterparty diversification, settlement instructions and periodic board-level reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Confirmation of Company Details) filed with the Commercial Court Registry (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the Infogreffe/Guichet unique portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after ordinary shareholders' meeting approving annual accounts; accounts must be approved within 6 months of fiscal year-end (standard rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to 1.8% of total annual revenue (first breach) or 3.6% for repeat breach; possible injunction; risk of judicial strike-off if no filing for 2 consecutive years

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes) filed with the Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via Guichet unique)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of shareholders' approval date; approval must occur within 6 months after fiscal year-end (extendable by court order)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to €9,000 per director; additional penalty for publication noncompliance; late filing penalties under tax law up to 5% of tax due with 10% surcharge if Denmark-EU reporting rules apply to audited accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individual Income Tax Return for Representatives (Director's tax return, if any) – not a corporate deliverable unless required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May–June depending on online filing department codes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines based on personal tax; not a corporate annual register filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation of Beneficial Owner (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs – DBE) annual re-certification if ownership changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in ownership/control; must be kept updated continuously, no fixed annual repeat if unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to €15,000 and/or 6 months imprisonment for non-disclosure (Lease-Sarran rules); administrative strike-off risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Franchise Tax on No-License or Non-Banking Activities – notably the CVAE (Cotisation sur la Valeur Ajoutée des Entreprises) if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CVAE declaration and payment due May 3 of the following year for fiscal year-end Dec 31; CVAE phased out for SMEs (effective exemption from 2023 for revenue < €500,000; suppressed from 2024 for all where no R&D assets)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge plus 5% late filing penalty; late payment interest at 0.2% monthly

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) if for the last fiscal year it surpasses two of three thresholds: total balance sheet > €4,000,000; net turnover (pré-HTL) > €8,000,000; average > 50 employees. Also mandatory if the SAS has a finance license or qualifies as a public-interest entity (not applicable here). A voluntary auditor may be appointed in the articles.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (PCG – Plan Comptable Général, ANC Regulation 2016-07); consolidated IFRS optional for groups; individual statutory accounts must comply with French GAAP

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must maintain a register of beneficial owners and file a Declaration of Beneficial Owners (DBE) with the Registry. For share transfers, file an updated DBE within 30 days of registration in the share transfer register. Annual confirmation not required solely on fixed anniversary unless a change occurs; the annual return form (Modalités de déclaration) confirms current shareholders and directors each year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)
Register of Directors' Meetings and Minutes
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: SAS: €1,200–€3,500 (professional registered office service) or €0 if using own premises
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: €6,500–€15,000 for a statutory audit; TSAR/compilation only €2,500–€5,000 if voluntary audit not engaged

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, 'IS') for fiscal years opened from 1 January 2022; qualifying SMEs with turnover not exceeding €10,000,000 benefit from a 15% reduced rate on the first €42,000 of net profit; large groups additionally pay a 3.3% social contribution on the IS where the annual IS liability exceeds €763,000, producing an effective marginal rate of 25.825%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research tax credit (CIR) at 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure up to €100,000,000 and 5% above, with immediate cash refund options for young innovative companies; patent-box regime under Article 238 CGI taxing qualifying intellectual-property income at a 10% effective rate; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% for SMEs; accelerated depreciation for certain digital assets; the SAS is mandatorily subject to entity-level IS and cannot elect partnership-style transparency.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite statutory carryforward (report en avant) with no time limit, but annual utilization capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above €1,000,000; loss carryback (report en arrière) has been abolished for fiscal years ending on or after 31 December 2024.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (CERFA No. 15950) annual result declaration (liasse fiscale) composed of Form 2065 and the 2050–2059 annex series, filed exclusively electronically through the DGFiP professional portal (declarer.impots.gouv.fr / EDI-EFI module); quarterly IS instalments are filed via Form 2571-SD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (liasse fiscale); quarterly instalments (acomptes) due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; balancing payment made with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ending 31 December: return due on the second working day following 1 May (e.g., 5 May 2025); fiscal year ending on any other date: return due within three months of the fiscal year close; electronic filers with calendar-year closings must pay the balance by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name of the SAS, SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code, company legal form, and head-office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact INPI/RCS-registered data; a 100% foreign-owned SAS remains a resident French taxpayer and files as a French legal entity, not as a branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirms the entity is taxed under the real-profit regime (régime réel normal) subject to IS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not select any transparency option; an SAS cannot opt for personal income-tax pass-through regardless of shareholder residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex 2053 – Lines 1/2 (Ventes de marchandises / Prestations de services)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues, net of French VAT, from voice-streaming subscriptions, virtual-gift sales, premium audio features, and advertising placed through the app.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross App Store and Google Play billing proceeds; Apple IAP and Google Play commissions must not be netted against revenue — claim them as deductible distribution/technical fees in Annex 2058-A with contractual support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Itemized deductible expenses: staff costs, cloud hosting and streaming bandwidth, content licensing, marketing, legal fees, and digital-platform commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow related-party payments lacking economic substance or contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation; maintain full invoicing from offshore data-processing and content providers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax credits including CIR, CII, and any other offsettable credits against French IS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot directly claim or refund CIR; credits are applied only against the SAS's own French IS liability and require eligible French R&D activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2257 – Contrôle des prix de transfert
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary declaration of intercompany transactions and transfer-pricing method applied, attached to the annual return by entities crossing the documentation threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for a foreign-controlled SAS engaged in cross-border related-party flows; material from the Local File and Master File must be reconciled with the figures reported on this form.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing under Article 1728 CGI: 10% surcharge where the return is filed late but within 30 days of formal notice, 40% where filed after 30 days or in bad faith, and 80% for fraudulent returns; late-payment interest of 0.20% per month under Article 1727 CGI; fixed penalty of €150 per omitted or inaccurate schedule, with additional €15-per-line corrections for balance-sheet annexes.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% gross withholding on dividends distributed by a French SAS to non-resident corporate shareholders under Article 119 bis 2 CGI; 12.8% flat-rate withholding (prélèvement forfaitaire unique) for non-resident individuals; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds at least 10% of the SAS for 24 months and is actually subject to corporate tax without an artificial arrangement; treaty-resident corporate shareholders typically qualify for 0–15% treaty rates, frequently 5% where a 10% or 25% holding test is met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a treaty or directive rate at source, the payor must hold a valid tax residence certificate (Formulaire 5000/5001) issued by the foreign tax authority before the payment date, together with a documentary statement of beneficial ownership, the shareholding percentage, and the holding period; EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief is granted upon receipt of a sworn attestation from the EU parent undertaking continued 10% ownership for two years and effective taxation; where the 25% or 12.8% domestic levy has been withheld, the non-resident beneficiary may claim a refund from the DGFiP by 31 December of the second calendar year following the distribution, under the claim procedure set out in Articles R.196-1 et seq. of the Livre des procédures fiscales.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: French domestic levy of 33.33% on industrial-property and copyright royalties paid to non-residents, generally reduced to 0–10% under double-tax agreements (commonly 5% for patents and similar rights, 0–5% for copyrighted software under recent treaties). Interest: arm's length interest paid by a French SAS to a non-resident EU/EEA lender is normally exempt from French withholding where the beneficial owner is a treaty-protected or directive-protected company not situated in a non-cooperative jurisdiction; outside that protection, a 25% (companies) or 12.8% (individuals) levy may apply under Articles 119 bis and 125 A CGI, with treaty rates generally capped at 0–10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400,000,000 (French-consolidated annual turnover or total balance-sheet assets) per Articles L.13 AA and L.13 AB CGI, triggering mandatory Local File, Master File, and Form 2257 disclosure; Country-by-Country Report required where the group reports consolidated revenue of at least €750,000,000; all cross-border controlled transactions must satisfy the arm's length standard under Article 57 CGI regardless of size.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not impose Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but applies a comprehensive substance doctrine: corporate tax residence is determined by the siège de direction effective (effective place of management) under Article 4 CGI, and Articles 209 and 238 CGI deny deductions or recharacterize structures lacking genuine local business purpose. The EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive (ATAD) CFC rules, the general anti-abuse doctrine of Article L.64 of the Livre des procédures fiscales, and the BEPS MLI principal purpose test require the SAS to demonstrate real local staff, premises, commercial decision-making, and actual voice-streaming service delivery; an SAS incorporated in France but managed from abroad for tax avoidance is exposed to recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, and recapture of incentives.
